title: Church Discipline and the Keys
lead: Jesus gave Peter and the disciples authority to "bind and loose" and set out steps for dealing with a member who sins. Churches have built on these words very different practices: confession and absolution, excommunication, the ban, and congregational discipline.

sections.b: Jesus gives Peter "the keys of the kingdom of heaven" and the power to bind and loose (Matthew 16:19), then gives binding and loosing to the disciples as a group, after a three-step process for a sinning brother: private correction, witnesses, the church (Matthew 18:15–18). In John 20:22–23 the risen Jesus gives the disciples power to forgive and retain sins. Paul tells Corinth to put out a man living in open sin, and later to forgive and comfort a man who repented (1 Corinthians 5:1–13; 2 Corinthians 2:5–11), and he tells the Thessalonians to keep apart from the disobedient but to warn him as a brother (2 Thessalonians 3:14–15). The background is Jewish: teachers "bound" and "loosed" what was forbidden and allowed, and the Dead Sea community had its own steps of rebuke and exclusion.
